title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Channel Persons
tiers.description: Directors, officers, employees, contractors or service providers of Channel Infrastructure or its subsidiaries. Subject to the fundamental insider trading rule, the short-term dealing guidance and the ban on hedging unvested equity-scheme entitlements, but no preclearance regime unless also a Restricted Person.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All Directors, the Chief Executive, all Leadership Team members and their direct reports, all Finance team members, and anyone else notified by the Company Secretary. Subject to Appendix I: blackout periods, prior written consent to trade at any time, and post-trade reporting.

tiers.name: Directors, Chief Executive or Company Secretary
tiers.description: Subset of Restricted Persons for whom the Request for Consent to trade must be signed by the Board Chair (or the Chair of the Audit and Finance Committee if the Chair is absent or is the one trading), rather than the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A Channel Person's spouse or partner, dependent children, family members or other persons acting on their direction, and companies, trusts or entities they control; Restricted Persons are responsible for the actions of their Associates.

definitions.hedging_definition: any transaction for any associated product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any unvested entitlement you are eligible for under that remuneration scheme

windows.end_anchor: first trading day after the release of the annual report to the NZX and ASX
first trading day after the release of the half-year preliminary announcement to the NZX and ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Company Secretary may specify any other blackout period from time to time (e.g. prior to a capital raising or refinancing). The policy does not state whether these ad hoc periods are confidential.

rules.detail: Company Securities includes options, derivatives or other financial products created over or in respect of the Company's listed financial products, with no venue limitation on the derivative itself, and 'trade' includes agreeing to buy or sell. Ordinary Channel Persons (not also Restricted Persons) face no preclearance system for dealing in derivatives, only the fundamental insider-trading prohibition and short-term dealing guidance.
rules.evidence: any options, derivatives or other financial products issued or created over or in respect of any financial products of Channel Infrastructure or its subsidiaries that are listed on a stock exchange

rules.detail: A derivative over Company Securities is itself a Company Security, so creating or dealing in one is a 'trade' requiring prior written consent from the Company Secretary (or Board Chair for Directors/CE/Company Secretary), outside blackout periods absent an Exceptional Circumstances waiver.
rules.evidence: Before trading Company Securities at any time outside of a black-out period, Restricted Persons must in writing: Notify the Company Secretary of their intention to trade Company Securities, and seek consent to do so

rules.detail: Absolute ban, applying to any Channel Person entitled to participate in an equity-based remuneration scheme, on associated-product transactions that limit the economic risk of an unvested entitlement.
rules.evidence: you may not enter into any transaction for any associated product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any unvested entitlement you are eligible for under that remuneration scheme

rules.detail: Once LTI/share-scheme securities vest and are issued, any trading (including hedging) is governed by the ordinary Securities Trading Policy, not by section 9's unvested ban; ordinary Channel Persons have no preclearance requirement.
rules.evidence: any trading in those Company Securities must only occur in accordance with this Securities Trading Policy

rules.detail: Hedging of vested securities by a Restricted Person is an ordinary 'trade' requiring prior written consent and compliance with blackout periods.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must also comply with Appendix I

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is a 'trade' because 'trade' includes agreeing to sell; for ordinary Channel Persons this only attracts the general insider-trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: 'trade' is a broad concept and includes buying or selling Company Securities or agreeing to do so

rules.detail: For a Restricted Person, an agreement to sell (such as a prepaid forward) is a trade requiring prior written consent and compliance with blackout periods.
rules.evidence: Before trading Company Securities at any time outside of a black-out period, Restricted Persons must in writing ... seek consent

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are not named but fall within 'other financial products issued or created over or in respect of' the Company's listed financial products; for ordinary Channel Persons only the general insider-trading rule applies.
rules.evidence: any options, derivatives or other financial products issued or created over or in respect of any financial products of Channel Infrastructure or its subsidiaries

rules.detail: A CFD over Company Securities is a Company Security and thus a trade requiring the Restricted Person consent process.
rules.evidence: Before trading Company Securities at any time outside of a black-out period, Restricted Persons must in writing ... seek consent

rules.detail: Margin lending is not addressed anywhere in the policy.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Company Securities is not addressed and is not swept into the broad 'trade' definition, which is framed around buying, selling and agreeing to do so.
Secured financing arrangements are not addressed anywhere in the policy.

Applies to all Channel Persons (not limited to Restricted Persons): no buying and selling of Company Securities within a 6-month period, unless the Company Secretary, in consultation with the Board Chair or Audit and Finance Committee Chair, approves exceptional circumstances.
rules.evidence: You should not engage in short term dealing (i.e. buying and selling Company Securities within a 6-month period) unless there are exceptional circumstances discussed and approved by the Company Secretary in consultation with the Chair of the Board or the Chair of the Audit and Finance Committee.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (contract note or other transaction documentation)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: 2 working days after the trade is completed
clearance.evidence: A consent to trade is only valid for a period of 10 trading days after notification (and a new consent is required for dealings in Company Securities which will be completed more than 10 trading days after a previous consent was given). A consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the Restricted Person acquires or becomes aware of Material Information prior to dealing.

clearance.tier: Directors, Chief Executive or Company Secretary
clearance.approver: Board Chair, or in their absence the Chair of the Audit and Finance Committee (Audit and Finance Committee Chair if the Board Chair is the one trading)
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (contract note or other transaction documentation)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: 2 working days after the trade is completed
clearance.evidence: In the case of the proposed trading by a Director, Chief Executive or the Company Secretary, the Request for Consent must be signed by the Board Chair, or in their absence, the Chair of the Audit and Finance Committee.

short_term.basis: buying and selling within the period
carve_outs: exceptional circumstances discussed and approved by the Company Secretary in consultation with the Chair of the Board or the Chair of the Audit and Finance Committee
short_term.evidence: You should not engage in short term dealing (i.e. buying and selling Company Securities within a 6-month period) unless there are exceptional circumstances discussed and approved by the Company Secretary in consultation with the Chair of the Board or the Chair of the Audit and Finance Committee.

exceptions.approver: Board Chair, or in their absence the Chair of the Audit and Finance Committee
exceptions.evidence: The Restricted Person is in severe financial hardship

exceptions.approver: Board Chair, or in their absence the Chair of the Audit and Finance Committee
exceptions.evidence: The Restricted Person is required by a court order or other court enforceable undertaking to transfer or sell Company Securities.
acquisitions and disposals by gift or inheritance

acquisitions through an issue of new quoted financial products, such as an issue of new CHI shares by the Company (for example, under a rights issue, dividend reinvestment plan or share purchase plan).

The additional trading restrictions set out above do not apply to participation in an employee, executive or director share scheme or Long-Term Incentive plan (LTI) operated by the Company (e.g. agreeing to participate in an LTI plan), or to share rights issued under a Share Rights Plan.

exemption_authority: Company Secretary may declare additional ad hoc blackout periods. During a blackout period, only the Board Chair (or Audit and Finance Committee Chair) may grant a specific exemption to trade, and only in Exceptional Circumstances (severe financial hardship or a court order), valid for 2 trading days from notification.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any options, derivatives or other financial products issued or created over or in respect of any financial products of Channel Infrastructure or its subsidiaries that are listed on a stock exchange
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The condition 'listed on a stock exchange' attaches to the underlying financial product (CHI's listed shares), not to the derivative itself, so an unlisted OTC put/call written by a bank over listed CHI shares is a Company Security and a 'trade' under this policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a Restricted Person must immediately provide the Company Secretary with the Common Shareholder Number/s and other personal information relating to their Channel Infrastructure holdings for their personal accounts and any other accounts that they control
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company Secretary can compel disclosure of any account (including one used to hold collared shares or post as collateral) that a Restricted Person controls, on request.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The FMCA requires Directors and senior managers to disclose all trades in Company Securities in which they have a relevant interest (as defined in the FMCA).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering or unwinding a collar and pledging shares as loan security will likely need separate substantial-holding/relevant-interest disclosure under the FMCA, on top of this policy's consent process.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no closed-period relief for ordinary trading
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are not permitted to deal in any Company Securities during a black-out period unless the Company Secretary provides a specific exemption in Exceptional Circumstances
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar execution, unwind or roll timed to fall inside a blackout window is blocked for Restricted Persons absent hardship or a court order, and any such waiver only lasts 2 trading days.

summary: A funded collar is workable for vested, unrestricted CHI shares, but the path differs sharply by tier. Ordinary Channel Persons who are not Restricted Persons face no preclearance system at all for a derivative or secured loan over vested shares (only the general insider-trading prohibition and a 6-month short-term dealing guideline), so a collar and loan could in principle be arranged freely once shares vest. Restricted Persons (directors, the CE, Leadership Team and direct reports, and Finance staff) must obtain prior written consent from the Company Secretary (or the Board Chair for Director/CE/Company Secretary trades), valid for only 10 trading days, and must not deal during the two annual blackout periods except under a hardship or court-order waiver valid for just 2 trading days. Hedging is expressly banned only over unvested equity-scheme entitlements, so it does not block a collar over already-vested shares. The policy is entirely silent on margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, forced sale and minimum shareholding, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares faces no express bar, though the definition of Company Securities is broad enough to catch an OTC derivative and would require Restricted Persons to obtain consent, execute within the window, and separately consider FMCA relevant-interest disclosure.
